correctness.rationale: The incidence identity \(B^\top B=(q-2)I+J\) proves P0 is an orthogonal projection and fixes every nonzero sign. The signed Kneser matrix \(S=2BB^\top-2I-J\) has eigenvalues alpha on constants, beta on E, -2 on W, giving exact all-m leakage identity (1), sharp via rank-one rotations. At \(m=4\) the entire local equality manifold is the hyperplanes of the 5D incidence space; positive row sums give strict weighted ascent off P0. The simple top eigenvalue 8/5 of |P0| has gap \(5/3\) to the E-mode, and its standard second derivative gives precisely \(48/125\) for every unit angular direction. The accompanying tested script returned 2330 supplementary checks; finite samples are not used in the proof.

originality.rationale: The closest published full text covers perturbing weights with the Gram matrix fixed and expressly excludes frame perturbations. The original arXiv source supplies the unperturbed frame; other full-text comparisons give global maximization, graph-eigenvalue, or ambient-dimension results. None of these statements logically covers the quantified local variable-projector landscape, flat \(m=4\) manifold together with strict weighted ascent and the exact quadratic gain. Standard spectral computations are acknowledged as ingredients; unindexed equivalent work remains a genuine risk.
residual_risks: The Sept 2026 Sidelnikov–Welch paper was verifiable at abstract level but its full text could not be retrieved in this session; its stated topic is recursive weighted frame inequalities, not local Gram perturbations.
An unindexed equivalent result in frame optimization or signed-graph spectral geometry might exist; searches do not prove novelty.

The leakage formula follows from classical spectral variational methods and known incidence eigenvalues; the mathematical contribution is the concrete sharp local classification and the weighted ascent, not those standard ingredients.

value.rationale: The edge-midpoint frames are explicit candidates in difficult maximal real projection-constant conjectures. Their local stability and optimizer geometry are natural tests of these candidates: the exact optimal Frobenius gap and equality modes resolve this for every dimension >=5, dimension 7 exhibits isotropic loss, and dimension 4 has a four-dimensional equal-weight plateau that becomes a strict ascent family once weights are optimized. The explicit \(48/125\) coefficient quantifies the mismatch between the two central frame functionals that agree at the source configuration. This is a motivated structural classification, not an arbitrary matrix slice or a claim of new global projection constants.
